quizName: Hardest Questions in Wisconsin Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash, keep you comfortable, and help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. You should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder and avoid traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors when riding to help other drivers see you, even during the day.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly all around your head and have no damage.

questions.question: When riding, the best gear to wear is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: What helps reduce head and neck injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up may make them follow you at the higher speed and increase danger.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign alerts you to watch for bicycles crossing the road.

questions.question: Your chances of surviving a crash improve if you wear:
questions.explanation: A properly fitted DOT-approved helmet gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good helmet is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: How do you sober up after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will sober you up. Your body needs time to remove the alcohol from your system. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green to be seen while riding. Bright colors help other drivers see you, no matter what time you ride.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator improve their visibility?
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Always use your headlight, signals, and brake light.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: Alcohol builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly causes alcohol to build up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is important even if you are borrowing the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are unsafe for motorcycles. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates all reduce traction. Dry pavement is safest.

questions.question: For the best helmet protection, choose a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: When riding, gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to grip the handgrips better.
Not be worn because they make controls harder to use.
Only be worn on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to grip the handgrips better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all around your head.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection to motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine even if it is under-inflated.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the bike's paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every motorcycle ride. Test your brakes to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually does not change how a motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for new riders.
Can change how a motorcycle handles.
Is a good way to help new riders learn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how a motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see better and be seen by others.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Allow other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also prevents other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let traffic safely merge.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see better and be seen by others.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also prevents other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear proper protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and strong gloves.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue, you should:
questions.explanation: Take rest breaks during long rides to fight fatigue. Caffeine may seem to help but can actually make fatigue worse when it wears off. Wind, rain, and cold also cause fatigue, so dress warmly and use a windshield for long rides.

questions.question: Reflective, bright-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not make motorcycle riders safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in and avoid being noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use turn signals, brake lights, and good lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to danger.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.explanation: Protection is your first concern when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You should not use them if no vehicles are near you.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use your turn signals when you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, position yourself where other drivers can see you most easily.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury?
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries, no matter how fast you ride.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: What is true about clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
It should not fully cover your arms or legs.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing provides important protection during a crash. Always wear a jacket and long pants to cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is fastened securely is the single best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: No, they do not have blind spots.
Mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do with shoelaces when riding?
questions.explanation: Tuck your shoelaces in securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: As part of your normal scanning routine.
They are not helpful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently as part of your normal search routine. Pay special attention to your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.
